Full detail: ADR-010.

sprint.name: Dynamic Master-Site Authoritative-Page Discovery + Program Relevance Gate + Master Page Index & Multi-Target Orchestration
sprint.note: Implemented, tested, typecheck/build clean, code-reviewed (/code-review high, 5 findings), and live-validated against two independent real master domains (Online Manipal and a second, unrelated real domain) on 2026-08-11. Four confirmed defects (C1-C4) found and fixed, each with a regression test, zero suite regressions. One real-world limitation (C5) acknowledged and documented, not fixed -- safety/relevance gates were not weakened. No real, 100-target, open-internet run was performed; the ~3-minute-at-100-targets figure remains a goal supported by extrapolation, not a direct measurement. Working tree is NOT committed or pushed as of this update.

known_issues: ln-pgcp-ei-mahe (one specific real URL) redirects (302) to the Master's bare homepage -- no reliable evidence exists there to resolve a specific program; correctly stays authoritative_page_not_found, investigated and documented, not fixed (not a resolution-logic defect -- a stale-URL/content problem on the real site).

Program Relevance Gate subject-overlap can still false-positive-tie across genuinely different subjects on the real Online Manipal site (ln-msc-ds-mahe) -- safe (ambiguous_candidates, never a wrong pick), same family as C5, not fixed.

PG-Certificate-style program naming (ln-pgcp-*) not recognized by degree-keywords.json -- an Understanding-layer (Sprint 2) gap, causes most of the ln-pgcp-* authoritative_page_not_found results in live validation.

Sprint 2 fact-extraction gaps confirmed still present on real pages during this session's comparison-output review: duration/mode/accreditation are frequently both_missing, and eligibility/fees occasionally capture a table-header label (e.g. "Full Fee Payment") instead of the actual value, on some real Online Manipal pages. Pre-existing, unrelated to and unaffected by the D1 fix; reported honestly, not fixed this session.

Institution vs. brand conflation (Sprint 2) is mitigated for REGISTERED institutions by Sprint 3's brand-alias fallback in resolveSource. Unregistered institutions still correctly report no_registry_entry, not a guess.

Heading-scoped claim extraction can grab a short label instead of the full sentence on real pages with nested sub-headings. Unrelated to Sprint 3/4/4b/5/5B/D1; still open, best-effort per Sprint 2's stated scope.

C5 (Sprint 5/5B, acknowledged, not fixed): real-world recall limitation on large, non-university-shaped sites -- system still never guesses wrong. Related, still-open gap: a same-domain candidate URL that redirects off-domain mid-fetch isn't re-checked against the domain boundary on its post-redirect destination.

A residual D1-adjacent gap remains, by design, for a target whose ONLY institution/brand signal (across URL, page text, and logo) is the generic shared brand identical to the wrong institution's own signal -- text/logo-based corroboration cannot distinguish that narrow case; closing it fully needs full MAHE/SMU Source registration or deeper extraction, both still open decisions. Not observed as the deciding factor in any of this session's real validation targets (URL tokens or real logo assets resolved every case that resolved at all).

Memory-file staleness has recurred multiple times across sessions -- always caught by cross-checking git log/git status/source directly rather than trusting memory at face value. Continue doing that at the start of every session.
